label: also exposed as
type: subject = a resource (typically a system-keyspace-style object such as system:active-requests); object = an alternative access surface for the SAME underlying resource, documented as a separate page/endpoint (typically a REST admin endpoint such as n1ql:query-admin-rest-api's /admin/active_requests). Declared range is deliberately loose: an access surface, not a fixed type, because the two sides so far are a SQL++ system keyspace and a REST endpoint - different kinds of thing exposing the same data.
instances: 0 concrete (no page states the identity outright); promoted on the strength of the proposal being independently raised twice, from both directions, with converging structural evidence
note:
PROMOTED UNDER THE SEMANTIC-SIGNIFICANCE EXCEPTION, NOT THE RECURRENCE RULE - said explicitly, per the reconciliation discipline that a predicate whose significance outweighs its recurrence can be promoted below the usual bar if the exception is stated rather than smuggled in as if it met the bar. Round 10's n1ql-rest-api/intro.json first proposed this predicate (alongside `hasAlternativeAccessSurface`) when it noticed /admin/active_requests, /admin/completed_requests, /admin/prepareds and /admin/vitals looked like REST mirrors of the system:active_requests / system:completed_requests / system:prepareds / system:vitals keyspaces, but could not act on its own proposal because it was reading only the REST side. Round 24's n1ql-rest-admin/index.json reads the REST side in full and finds the SAME structural match independently, from the object-schema level down: the admin Requests object's `clientContextID` field cites the exact request-level `client_context_id` parameter by name, its `cpuTime` field cites the exact `execTime`-sum definition from the query-plan reference, its `scanConsistency` field cites the exact 'Scan Consistency' query setting - the same fields the monitoring/system-keyspace pages already document for the SQL++ side, described here from the REST side instead.
WHY THIS IS PROMOTED WITHOUT A SINGLE CONCRETE INSTANCE. No page anywhere states 'this endpoint returns the same data as system:X' as a sentence - the identity is a structural inference from matching field definitions, not a quoted claim, and minting a concrete triple from an inference rather than a quote would violate the evidence discipline this whole project runs on. What IS promotable is the schema-level predicate itself: two independent rounds, reading from two different sides of the same gap eight rounds apart, converged on needing the identical missing predicate to name the identical missing relation. That convergence is the evidence for the PREDICATE's existence, even though it cannot yet license any INSTANCE of it. Should a future round find a page that states the identity outright, this predicate is ready to receive its first concrete triple without needing to be minted at that point.
WHAT IT COVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It names 'same resource, alternate surface' in general - not specifically the REST/SQL++ pair above, which is only the case that forced the mint. It should NOT be used for two pages that merely document the same FEATURE from two angles (that is ordinary cross-page corroboration, no predicate needed); it is for two pages that expose access to the SAME underlying object/dataset through two structurally different interfaces.
